title: Task sensitivity profiles and composite scoring engine for FP8/INT8 validation
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement a composite scoring engine and per-task sensitivity profiles for validating FP8 and INT8 quantized profiles. The goal is to produce actionable, statistically robust quality signals for runtime rollouts and automated gating. This ticket covers metric selection (perplexity variants, MMLU-style micro/macro aggregates, BLEU/ROUGE with smoothing and length-normalization), task-specific scorers (classification accuracy/F1, ranking MRR/NDCG, summarization ROUGE-L), and the composite score algorithm that combines them into a single rollout-ready index with confidence intervals and compute cost-awareness.
acceptance_criteria: Implement token-level perplexity computation that is stable across byte-pair tokenizers and reports delta vs FP32 baseline
Provide MMLU-style micro and macro aggregations with per-task sample weighting and bootstrap confidence intervals
Implement BLEU and ROUGE variants with configurable smoothing and length-penalty parameters; expose per-example and corpus-level outputs
Create a pluggable task-scorer API for classification, multiple-choice, ranking, and summarization tasks
Expose a composite score that combines normalized metrics (z-score or percentile-based), includes an uncertainty term, and allows latency/compute weighting
Integrate outputs into the eval harness and Redwood Console dashboard with per-route breakdowns and alert thresholds
Document gating rules for canary rollouts: exact thresholds, CI methods, minimum sample sizes, and fallbacks
implementation_notes: Perplexity: compute token-level negative log-likelihood, normalize by effective token count, and report per-sequence and aggregated geometric mean; add delta_perplexity = (quant - fp32) / fp32
MMLU: compute per-subject accuracy, then report macro average and micro average; bootstrap 10k samples for 95% CI but make sample size configurable to reduce compute
BLEU/ROUGE: use sacrebleu-style tokenization for BLEU and Rouge-L for summarization; include smoothing=exp and smoothing=method2 options
Task scorers: classification => accuracy, precision/recall/F1 (macro, weighted); ranking => MRR@k and NDCG@k; summarization => ROUGE-1/2/L F1 and coverage metrics
Composite score: normalize each metric into a 0-1 scale using baseline FP32 means and stdevs; allow alternative normalization (percentile mapping); combine with tunable weights per-project
Uncertainty: use bootstrap to compute metric variance; composite includes uncertainty penalty (e.g., score - z*std) to avoid noisy rollouts
Compute-cost weighting: attach per-eval token or latency cost estimate and allow weighted combination so cost-sensitive teams can trade accuracy for performance
Canary gating: require both point estimate and CI lower bound above threshold OR pass relative delta thresholds on key metrics
Data splits: ensure evaluation uses holdout test sets, stratified by task, and preserve original input distributions to avoid selection bias
Performance: vectorize metric computations, use batched tensor ops for likelihoods; fall back to sampled bootstrap for huge corpora
